**Comparability note:** Alaska Air Group's FY2024 figures include Hawaiian Holdings' results only from the September 18, 2024 acquisition date forward (contributing $869M revenue and a $113M net loss) [DOC-2]. This means Alaska's FY2024 cost/revenue ratios reflect a partial-year, post-acquisition blend rather than a full year of comparable operations, so its efficiency metrics are not strictly comparable to the other four carriers, which report full-year, non-acquisition-affected results [DOC-1].

**Analysis of cost efficiency (using operating margin and fuel+labor cost as % of revenue):**

Operating margin (Operating income ÷ Total operating revenue) [DOC-1]:
- Delta: $5,995M / $61,643M = 9.7%
- United: $5,096M / $57,063M = 8.9%
- American: $2,614M / $54,211M = 4.8%
- Alaska: $570M / $11,735M = 4.9% (partial-year Hawaiian impact per [DOC-2])
- Southwest: $321M / $27,483M = 1.2%

Combined fuel + labor costs as % of revenue [DOC-1]:
- Delta: ($10,566M + $16,161M) / $61,643M = 43.4%
- United: ($11,756M + $16,678M) / $57,063M = 49.8%
- American: ($11,418M + $16,021M) / $54,211M = 50.6%
- Alaska: ($2,506M + $3,588M) / $11,735M = 51.9%
- Southwest: ($5,812M + $12,240M) / $27,483M = 65.7%

Delta Air Lines had both the highest operating margin (9.7%) [DOC-1] and the lowest combined fuel-and-labor cost ratio (43.4% of revenue) [DOC-1] among the five carriers, indicating the most efficient cost structure in FY2024. Southwest, by contrast, had by far the highest cost ratios and lowest operating margin, suggesting the least efficient cost structure among the group in FY2024 [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines had the most efficient cost structure in FY2024, with the highest operating margin (~9.7%) and lowest combined fuel-and-labor expense ratio (~43.4% of revenue) among the five carriers; note that Alaska's results are not fully comparable due to the partial-year inclusion of the Hawaiian Holdings acquisition.
